headline: The US 10 year Treasury yield touched 5 percent for the first time since 2023 with futures pricing about 90 percent odds of a Fed rate hike on Wednesday, while a weekend call from three AI company chiefs to slow frontier model development pulled money out of chipmakers and into software and cybersecurity.

summary.us: The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,656.98 and the Nasdaq at 26,333.04 after August core CPI rose 0.3 percent month on month against a 0.2 percent forecast, lifting the odds of a quarter point hike at the 16 September FOMC to about 90 percent and taking the 10 year yield to 4.954 percent on Friday and through 5 percent on Monday. On Monday the tape split along AI lines after Anthropic's Dario Amodei argued that AI companies must slow the pace of capability gains, with Sam Altman and Elon Musk agreeing, sending Nvidia, Arm, Broadcom, Intel and the chip equipment names lower while Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and cybersecurity names including CrowdStrike rose.
summary.india: Nifty 50 closed Friday at 23,398.10, down 0.34 percent, and the Sensex at 74,781.76, as Brent above $100 on West Asia supply disruption hit metals, realty, auto and energy, while Bank Nifty closed 0.24 percent higher at 56,606 and India VIX rose above 12. Foreign institutional investors sold Rs 930.90 crore in the cash segment against domestic institutional buying of Rs 1,968.20 crore, and the rupee traded near 95.5 per dollar after touching 95.2250 earlier in the month on reported Reserve Bank of India intervention.
summary.global: The Nikkei closed Friday at 64,011 and fell a further 0.81 percent on Monday to 63,492.99 as the AI hardware selloff reached Asian suppliers, while Hang Seng rose 0.45 percent to 24,917.60 and the Shanghai Composite was little changed at 3,885.33. European markets closed higher on Friday, with the DAX up 0.82 percent to 25,569 led by Infineon, Siemens and Deutsche Telekom and UK gross domestic product beating expectations, before chip equipment weakness pulled the DAX back on Monday.
